tier1.text: Lipid droplets store lipids, a group that includes fats and oils, inside cells. White fat cells hold their lipids in one large drop, while brown fat cells hold many droplets. Heart muscle cells also store droplets of fatty acids, parts of fat molecules, as an extra supply of nutrients. Each droplet's lipids are wrapped in a single layer of phospholipids, the main part of membranes.

quotes.quote: The brown adipocytes store lipids as many droplets, and have high metabolic activity. In contrast, white fat adipocytes store lipids as a single large drop and are metabolically less active.

quotes.quote: A fat molecule consists of two main components—glycerol and fatty acids.

quotes.quote: An intracellular non-membrane-bounded organelle comprising a matrix of coalesced lipids surrounded by a phospholipid monolayer.
phospholipid: membranes' major constituent; comprised of two fatty acids and a phosphate-containing group attached to a glycerol backbone
quotes.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.
